📜 The Peruvian Congress included in the text of the 2027 Budget—approved on Friday, November 20—a provision that exempts the Executive Branch, led by Keiko Fujimori, from requiring the specific work experience established in Law 31419 for the appointment of public officials and executives who may be freely appointed and removed throughout the upcoming fiscal year. ⚖️ The measure suspends only the specific experience requirement set forth in Articles 4 and 5 of that law on eligibility and its implementing regulations, while maintaining the requirements for academic qualifications and general work experience. 🗣️ Congresswoman Indira Huilca questioned the provision, warning that it could encourage political patronage, and criticized the relaxation of requirements for access to positions of trust while demands from retired teachers, assistance for victims in Condorcanqui, and salary increases for basic services remain unaddressed.

Visioner BIG | 🇵🇱 🇺🇦 🇷🇺 ‼️ ‼️ Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski has declared that Russia is failing to achieve its military objectives in Ukraine, claiming Moscow has suffered nearly 50,000 troop losses in a single month without securing the major territorial gains it sought. Sikorski argued that Russia’s attacks on Ukrainian civilians will not break the country’s resistance, drawing parallels with the bombing of Coventry, London, Dresden, and Hamburg during World War II. He suggested Putin may be counting on winter conditions to weaken Ukraine. The Polish minister stressed that a lasting peace must begin with a ceasefire, pointing to previous localized arrangements around the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and Oleshky. He also noted ongoing prisoner and remains exchanges in Abu Dhabi, emphasizing that mediators, including Turkey, India, Switzerland, the UN, and the Pope, are available. Sikorski accused Moscow of rejecting Ukraine’s calls for an unconditional ceasefire and expressed hope that Washington and Beijing would increase pressure on Putin. Sikorski’s assessment highlights the growing gap between Russia’s costly offensive operations and its limited territorial achievements. His central argument is that Moscow’s continued bombardment of civilians reflects a strategy of coercion rather than a path to military victory. With diplomatic channels already functioning, he maintains that the principal obstacle to a broader ceasefire is the Kremlin’s unwillingness to end its war.
